questions.prompt: State the sine addition formula for \(\sin(A+B)\).
questions.answer:
The formula is
\[\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B.\]
It rewrites the sine of a sum using trig functions of the separate angles.

questions.prompt: State the cosine addition formula for \(\cos(A+B)\).
questions.answer:
The formula is
\[\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.\]
The minus sign is essential.

questions.prompt: Use an addition formula to expand \(\sin(x+\frac\pi6)\).
questions.answer:
Use \(\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B\):
\[\sin\left(x+\frac\pi6\right)=\sin x\cos\frac\pi6+\cos x\sin\frac\pi6.\]
Since \(\cos\frac\pi6=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) and \(\sin\frac\pi6=\frac12\),
\[\sin\left(x+\frac\pi6\right)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin x+\frac12\cos x.\]

questions.prompt: Use a difference formula to expand \(\cos(x-\frac\pi3)\).
questions.answer:
Use \(\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\):
\[\cos\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)=\cos x\cos\frac\pi3+\sin x\sin\frac\pi3.\]
Therefore
\[\cos\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)=\frac12\cos x+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin x.\]

questions.prompt: Use exact values to find \(\sin\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi6\right)\).
questions.answer:
Use the sine addition formula:
\[\sin\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi6\right)=\sin\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6+\cos\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6.\]
Substitute values:
\[=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.\]

questions.prompt: Use exact values to find \(\cos\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi6\right)\).
questions.answer:
Use the cosine addition formula:
\[\cos\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi6\right)=\cos\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6-\sin\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6.\]
So
\[=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.\]

questions.prompt: Derive the double-angle formula for \(\sin(2A)\) from the sine addition formula.
questions.answer:
Start with
\[\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B.\]
Set \(B=A\):
\[\sin(A+A)=\sin A\cos A+\cos A\sin A.\]
Thus
\[\sin(2A)=2\sin A\cos A.\]

questions.prompt: Use a double-angle formula to find \(\sin(2x)\) if \(\sin x=\frac35\) and \(\cos x=\frac45\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\sin(2x)=2\sin x\cos x.\]
Substitute:
\[\sin(2x)=2\left(\frac35\right)\left(\frac45\right)=\frac{24}{25}.\]

questions.prompt: Use the tangent addition formula to simplify \(\tan(A+B)\) when \(\tan A=2\) and \(\tan B=\frac13\).
questions.answer:
The tangent addition formula is
\[\tan(A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}.\]
Substitute:
\[\tan(A+B)=\frac{2+1/3}{1-2/3}=\frac{7/3}{1/3}=7.\]

questions.prompt: Use the cosine double-angle formula to find \(\cos(2x)\) if \(\cos x=\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\sin x=\frac{12}{13}\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\cos(2x)=\cos^2x-\sin^2x.\]
Then
\[\cos(2x)=\left(\frac5{13}\right)^2-\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)^2=\frac{25-144}{169}=-\frac{119}{169}.\]

questions.prompt: Show that \(\cos(2A)=2\cos^2A-1\).
questions.answer:
Start with
\[\cos(2A)=\cos^2A-\sin^2A.\]
Use \(\sin^2A=1-\cos^2A\):
\[\cos(2A)=\cos^2A-(1-\cos^2A).\]
So
\[\cos(2A)=2\cos^2A-1.\]

questions.prompt: Show that \(\cos(2A)=1-2\sin^2A\).
questions.answer:
Start with
\[\cos(2A)=\cos^2A-\sin^2A.\]
Use \(\cos^2A=1-\sin^2A\):
\[\cos(2A)=(1-\sin^2A)-\sin^2A.\]
Therefore
\[\cos(2A)=1-2\sin^2A.\]

questions.prompt: Find \(\tan(2x)\) if \(\tan x=\frac12\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\tan(2x)=\frac{2\tan x}{1-\tanan^2x}.\]
Substitute \(\tan x=\frac12\):
\[\tan(2x)=\frac{2(1/2)}{1-(1/2)^2}=\frac1{1-1/4}=\frac1{3/4}=\frac43.\]

questions.prompt: Find \(\cos\left(\frac\pi{12}\right)\) by writing \(\frac\pi{12}=\frac\pi4-\frac\pi6\).
questions.answer:
Use \(\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\):
\[\cos\frac\pi{12}=\cos\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6+\sin\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6.\]
Substitute exact values:
\[=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.\]

questions.prompt: Use a half-angle formula to find \(\sin\left(\frac\pi8\right)\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\sin\frac A2=\pm\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos A}{2}}.\]
Let \(A=\frac\pi4\). Since \(\frac\pi8\) is in quadrant I, choose the positive root:
\[\sin\frac\pi8=\sqrt{\frac{1-\sqrt2/2}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}}{2}.\]

questions.prompt: For which values of \(A\) is the formula \(\tan(2A)=\frac{2\tan A}{1-\tanan^2A}\) undefined because of its denominator?
questions.answer:
The displayed formula has denominator \(1-\tanan^2A\). It is zero when
\[1-\tanan^2A=0,\]
so
\[\tan^2A=1,\qquad \tan A=\pm1.\]
Thus the formula is undefined at
\[A=\frac\pi4+\frac{k\pi}{2},\quad k\in\mathbb Z,\]
where \(2A\) lands at an angle with undefined tangent.

questions.prompt: A student writes \(\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\). Diagnose the mistake using \(A=B=\frac\pi4\).
questions.answer:
The correct formula is
\[\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.\]
If \(A=B=\frac\pi4\), then \(A+B=\frac\pi2\), so \(\cos(A+B)=0\).
The student's formula gives
\[\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\frac{\sqrt2}{2}=1,\]
which is false. The sign should be negative.

questions.prompt: Prove the identity \(\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)=2\sin A\cos B\).
questions.answer:
Use the formulas
\[\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B\]
and
\[\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B.\]
Add them:
\[\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)=2\sin A\cos B+0.\]
Therefore the identity is true.

questions.prompt: Prove the identity \(\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)=2\sin A\sin B\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\]
and
\[\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.\]
Subtract:
\[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)=2\sin A\sin B.\]
The \(\cos A\cos B\) terms cancel.

questions.prompt: The displacement of a simple oscillator is \(x(t)=R\cos(\omega t+\phi)\). Expand it into a sum involving \(\cos(\omega t)\) and \(\sin(\omega t)\), and identify the coefficients.
questions.answer:
Use
\[\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.\]
With \(A=\omega t\) and \(B=\phi\),
\[x(t)=R[\cos(\omega t)\cos\phi-\sin(\omega t)\sin\phi].\]
So
\[x(t)=(R\cos\phi)\cos(\omega t)-(R\sin\phi)\sin(\omega t).\]
The coefficients are \(R\cos\phi\) for \(\cos(\omega t)\) and \(-R\sin\phi\) for \(\sin(\omega t)\).
